taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Market-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 104 | 2.86 | 2.86
2 | 186 | 2.38 | 5.24
3 | 266 | 24.7 | 29.9
4 | 327 | 24.6 | 54.6
5 | 219 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AAK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Market-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Market-road, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation shows a five-layer subsurface sequence with resistivity increasing from 104 Ω·m (layer 1, 0–2.86 m) to 186 Ω·m (layer 2, to 5.24 m) and 266 Ω·m (layer 3, to 29.9 m), continuing to rise to a maximum of 327 Ω·m (layer 4, to 54.6 m), before dropping to 219 Ω·m in the basal layer (layer 5, unconstrained thickness).

Applying the curve-type notation: layers 1-2-3 (104<186<266) give A; layers 2-3-4 (186<266<327) give A; layers 3-4-5 (266<327>219) give K. This yields a curve type of AAK, consistent with the progressively resistive near-surface sequence underlain by a more conductive basal unit.

The on-file classification (AAK-type) matches the computed sequence from the layer resistivity data. No discrepancy was found.

{"curve_type_stated": "AAK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
